title: penstemon marcusii
intro: Penstemon marcusii, commonly known as Marcus' beardtongue, is a species of flowering plant in the family Plantaginaceae. This perennial herb is native to the southwestern United States and Mexico, known for its tubular, red, purple, or pink flowers that attract pollinators. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties that may help to soothe respiratory issues and wounds. The bioactive constituents of Penstemon marcusii include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and iridoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, including antioxidant and antispasmodic effects.
